findings.scenario: A participant creates or controls many anonymous/pseudonymous accounts and submits once through each, multiplying influence despite the per-viewer limit.
findings.gap: Eligible-viewer identity, admission, and account-to-influence binding are unspecified; N-to-K does not itself constrain Sybils.
findings.recommendation: Bind one influence unit to a privacy-preserving authenticated platform subject per turn; set admission and aggregate caps, and keep bot identities separate.

findings.scenario: A coordinated group shards submissions across cohorts or manipulates the eligible denominator while K or tie rules are configurable, steering normalization without exceeding any one cohort's apparent cap.
findings.gap: Cohort assignment, roster timing, normalization denominator, quorum, and tie handling are unresolved.
findings.recommendation: Freeze eligible roster and cohort assignments before each turn; specify denominator, minimum participation, per-cohort caps, and deterministic tie handling.

findings.scenario: A bot-heavy group repeatedly backfills participation or induces wipe/survival outcomes that create or enlarge a simulated bounty, then routes value to an attacker-controlled eligible viewer.
findings.gap: Bot rewards are prohibited, but bounty provenance, creation authority, trigger accounting, and bot influence on bounty adjustments remain open.
findings.recommendation: Require explicit human authorization and traceable source for each bounty; exclude bots from funding, eligibility, and payout, and cap adjustments across retries and wipes.

findings.scenario: The attacker reapplies the bounded hazard on successive turns, consuming every counter window and leaving no practical recovery before the deadline.
findings.gap: No permanent control loss or unavoidable death is stated, but frequency, cumulative pressure, cooldown, and guaranteed recovery are not defined.
findings.recommendation: Set per-phase and match-wide pressure caps, cooldowns, non-stacking effects, and a guaranteed recovery or counter window independent of viewer turnout.

findings.scenario: A late chat message contains instructions aimed at the language model to propose an out-of-phase or stronger action; it is mistaken for control text rather than untrusted viewer content.
findings.gap: Natural language is only a proposal and local validation is required, but the prompt/data boundary and strict action mapping are not specified.
findings.recommendation: Treat chat as untrusted data, never as instructions; map it only to an enumerated action schema and enforce phase, eligibility, and effect bounds locally after model output.

findings.scenario: A reconnect or offline replay resubmits a previously accepted event under a new request and applies its influence twice, possibly in a later turn.
findings.gap: Duplicate and late input should be rejected/idempotent, but durable deduplication scope and session/turn binding are unspecified.
findings.recommendation: Use stable event IDs with durable deduplication bound to session and turn; reject stale sequence numbers and ensure replay cannot mint a new eligible event.
